about: Fixed settings for every video from the app's inbox (v3/inbox.py, .github/workflows/inbox.yml). best = run 4's recipe (the owner's best: ~420 frames, 1440 px, 30k steps, 1.5M splats); run 6 (900 frames, 1920 px, 40k, 3M) looked worse to the owner (28 Oct). quick = a short test run (end-to-end check, not for viewing). 'best' and 'home' size every run from the video itself (AUTO_STEPS) and from the time left in the Kaggle session (final/budget.py, 16 Nov): frames follow the camera's motion at run 4's density (411 per 123 s of walking, at most 1,000 and never more than the camera solve can finish in its share), splats by floor area (1.5 M per 37 m2, 1.5-4 M), steps by training views (83.6 each). A full-size dry run measures speed and memory; if run 4's recipe does not fit the session the job steps down (fewer steps per view, then fewer pixels, then every k-th frame, last a 7k preview) instead of stopping with nothing. The trainer stops itself at its deadline and keeps the model; a snapshot goes to Hugging Face at every checkpoint. Each run writes what it chose to budget.json. OBJECTS=1 (best, home): after training, if 40 min are left, the object layer and the search index for the tour's "find anything" (final/objects3d.py, ai_find.py). Extra env: DEADLINE_H (default 11.25), FRAME_PICK=time (old equal time windows), CHALLENGER=<kind> (an alternative recipe on the second T4, kept only if it scores better), NAMMA_REF (code branch for a test run).

home.note: same rules as best (sized from the video); kept as a name the app may send

fast.note: a room in minutes (26 Nov, branch claude/fast-train; not the default): at most 300 frames for a 5-minute walk, one short training with the fast recipe (final/fast_patch.py: fused colour grid, half-size pictures for the first 60 % of the steps, dense start from depth maps: final/dense_init.py), mesh from 100 cameras beside the object layer. Measured on the switch room (speed run 1, v3/SPEED.json, 270 training frames, same 116 held-out frames as the 30.59 dB / 3.4 h model): 15,000 steps = 18.7 min of training, 29.66 dB, SSIM 0.945, 9 % needles; 7,000 steps = 8.5 min, 29.22 dB, SSIM 0.937, 2 % needles (FAST_STEPS). Without the dense start 15,000 steps gave 28.95 dB and 16 % needles. 'best' is unchanged.
